writing_sample_excerpt: I used to think reading was boring until Ms. Reyes gave me 'Holes' and I read it in two days. The way Stanley keeps a notebook in the desert reminded me of how I write in my journal at night. I want to try writing my own story this summer.

notes: Counselor 2/12: student disclosed father in outpatient rehab; parent asked teacher not to mention home situation on report card.
writing_sample_excerpt: My dad came back from rehab last spring and we still don't really talk about it. Writing about it in this essay is the first time I have said the word out loud, even though no one will hear me say it. I think my mom is finally sleeping again.

Helping my grandma cook on Sundays is the best part of my week. She speaks mostly Igbo and I speak mostly English but somehow we always understand the recipe. The jollof rice is never the same twice and that is the whole point.

disciplinary_notes: Two write-ups in February for verbal conflict during lunch — restorative-justice circle held; situation resolved.
notes: Counselor 1/28: ICE contact on file; family immigration case active — treat all writing about brother as highly confidential.
writing_sample_excerpt: when my brother got deported, my mom stopped sleeping. I am the one who walks my little sister to school now. I am only twelve but I feel like I am thirty some days. Books are the only place I get to be a kid again.
Last summer my abuela taught me how to make tamales from scratch. I learned that patience is its own ingredient. I think writing essays is the same way — you cannot rush the corn husk.

notes: Nurse+counselor 9/3: new ADHD diagnosis; medication adjustment in progress. Do not reference meds or diagnosis in parent-facing comments.
writing_sample_excerpt: i was diagnosed with adhd over the summer and the meds make me feel weird sometimes. school is easier now but also kind of quieter in my head, which is strange. i still like science class the most because experiments don't care if my brain is fast or slow.

My favorite book this quarter was 'Inside Out and Back Again' by Thanhha Lai. The poems felt like the way I actually think — short and sideways. I want to try writing poems in Somali next, but I don't know the words for some feelings yet.

disciplinary_notes: Documented bullying target in October; counselor monitoring.
notes: Counselor 10/8: bullying incident Oct; restorative plan in place. Avoid naming other students or incident details externally.
writing_sample_excerpt: I started a journal in October because Ms. Patel in the counseling office said it might help. At first it was just dates and sad faces. Now there are paragraphs and even a poem. I am proud of that.

My dad and I are reading 'The Hobbit' out loud together — one chapter every Sunday morning. He does all the dwarf voices and I do Bilbo. It takes us almost an hour because we keep laughing and starting over.

writing_sample_excerpt: I used to hate writing because my brain moves faster than my pencil. This year I tried voice-to-text on the iPad and it changed everything. Now my essays sound like me when I talk, which I like.

disciplinary_notes: Suspended one day in January for fighting on bus.
notes: Counselor 1/15: bus fight suspension; anger-management check-ins weekly. Parent prefers no discipline labels on report card.
writing_sample_excerpt: I am working on not getting in trouble. Mr. Davis from PE said anger is just energy with nowhere to go, so I started running before school. It is helping. I am sorry for the bus thing — I really am.

notes: Counselor 11/2: mother's cancer treatment; student primary caregiver after school. Extreme sensitivity around health disclosures.
writing_sample_excerpt: after my mom's mastectomy I helped with her drains and that was my whole november. I learned more about being a person in those four weeks than in any class. She is okay now. I would write a whole book about her if I could.

notes: Counselor 3/4: housing instability risk flagged; brother autism morning routine. Tardies context is medical/family, not defiance.
writing_sample_excerpt: I know I am late a lot. The mornings are hard at my house because my little brother has autism and getting him out the door takes everything we have. I am not making excuses, just explaining.

Speech class on Tuesdays is my favorite even though some kids think it is babyish. My speech teacher Ms. Cohen is teaching me to slow down so my words come out the way I mean them. I am getting better.

disciplinary_notes: Caught with a vape in November; restorative consequence completed.
notes: Counselor 11/18: vape incident; family therapy started. Student ashamed — do not surface substance discipline on report card.
writing_sample_excerpt: Last quarter was bad. I made some choices I am not proud of. I have been talking to my mom more and we are going to family therapy on Wednesdays now. Writing this down is part of trying to do better.

I read 47 books this quarter. My favorite was 'A Wrinkle in Time' because Meg has trouble with people too and it works out for her. I am writing my own story about a girl who can hear what plants are thinking. It is going to be 200 pages.

My little sister and I share a bedroom and we built a reading fort with blankets and flashlights. We read 'Charlotte's Web' together and I cried at the end even though I am almost a teenager. I think caring about characters is a kind of bravery.
Basketball practice is the only part of the day where my brain goes quiet. Coach says discipline on the court shows up in the classroom too. I am trying to prove him right this quarter.

notes: Counselor 8/30: recent move; ESL support tier 2. Anxiety in new school — avoid comparative ranking language.
writing_sample_excerpt: We moved here in August and everything still feels temporary — new house, new friends, new lunch table. Writing in English is easier than speaking it because I can erase. I am proud I finished this essay without asking my mom for help.

disciplinary_notes: Three tardies in March — parent conference scheduled.
notes: Counselor 3/11: morning tardies; stepdad night shift. CPS inquiry closed 2025-11 — handle home references carefully.
writing_sample_excerpt: My stepdad works nights so mornings are loud and rushed. I am not trying to be late, I swear. I like this class because Ms. Reyes lets us write about real stuff instead of made-up prompts.

Cooking with my dad on weekends taught me that recipes are just instructions you can argue with. I rewrote a poem three times because the first version sounded like a recipe and the third version sounded like me.
People talk fast in the hallways and I catch every third word. In writing I can take my time and say exactly what I mean. This essay took me four drafts and I think that is okay.
My horse Scout got colic in January and we almost lost her. I wrote about the night we stayed up in the barn and how fear feels like cold hands. Scout is fine now. I still check on her before school.

disciplinary_notes: Phone confiscated twice in February for filming in hallway.
notes: Counselor 2/14: phone policy violations; ADHD screening waitlist. Creative strengths mask organization struggles.
writing_sample_excerpt: I make short videos for fun — not during class, I know the rules. This quarter I tried writing a script instead of filming and it was harder than I expected. Turns out dialogue is weird on paper.
Ramadan this year fell during state testing week and I was tired every morning. I wrote about fasting as patience practice. My friends asked questions and I liked explaining instead of hiding.
The quiet room for tests actually helps. I used to think needing extra time meant I was dumb. Ms. Reyes said slow and careful beats fast and sloppy. I am starting to believe her.

notes: Counselor 2/20: parents financial stress; student translating bills at home. Watch for anxiety spikes before assessments.
writing_sample_excerpt: My parents argue about money in Arabic and I pretend I am asleep. I wrote this essay in English because that is the language of school, but some feelings only exist in Arabic. Maybe next time I will try both.

disciplinary_notes: Detention in January for disrupting class — agreed to check in with counselor biweekly.
notes: Counselor 1/9: detention pattern tied to undiagnosed learning frustration; eval referral pending.
writing_sample_excerpt: I act out when I am confused because asking for help feels like admitting defeat. This essay was about the first time I raised my hand and the answer was wrong and nobody laughed. That mattered more than being right.

I volunteer at the animal shelter on Saturdays. The dogs do not care about grades. I wrote about a pit bull named Rusty who waited six months for adoption. I cried in front of the whole class and it was fine.

Lunch is the hardest period because the cafeteria is loud and nobody saves seats. I eat in the library on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I wrote about building a routine that works instead of pretending lunch is easy.

notes: Counselor 4/2: grandmother primary caregiver evenings; immigration history in family narrative — not for external docs.
writing_sample_excerpt: My grandma watches me after school while my mom works doubles at the diner. She tells stories about crossing the border that I am only old enough now to understand. This essay is for her, even though she cannot read English.

notes: Counselor 10/21: family lost housing Oct; now doubled up with aunt. FERPA-sensitive; student only recently disclosed to teacher.
writing_sample_excerpt: We lost our apartment in October and stayed with my aunt for two months. I did not tell anyone at school until Ms. Reyes asked how I was doing and actually waited for an answer. Having one adult who knows helps.
Presentations make my chest tight so I asked to record mine instead of standing up. Ms. Reyes said yes. The video was shaky but the words were mine. I am counting that as growth.

disciplinary_notes: One lunch detention in March for throwing food — apology letter completed.
notes: Counselor check-in 3/1: no acute concerns; routine wellness visit logged.
writing_sample_excerpt: I thought this assignment was dumb until I started writing about my grandfather's workshop. He builds furniture without nails. Patience again. Maybe essays and woodworking are the same skill.

I learned ukulele on YouTube during the winter break. Three chords are enough for most pop songs. I wrote about how music is easier to share than feelings, which is why I play for my little brother when he is scared at night.
